title: Arctic Trek A-Z
hook: Land, ice, water tell us how to travel next.
roundStructure: Round 1 lexical-semantic A-Z; Round 2 retrieval-action A-Z; 4+4+4+4+4+4+2 chunks
responseSpace: one-beat cue gap with backing thinned
visualStyle: friendly 3D arctic explorer storybook, simple map-and-snow mood, bright parkas and blue ice, clean objects

creativeFingerprint.pointOfView: a child on a supervised Arctic learning expedition where terrain determines travel mode and wildlife sets distance rules
creativeFingerprint.chorusFunction: restate map-route-change and prepare the next terrain transition
creativeFingerprint.round1Grammar: hand-written route progression; travel objects have real functions and animals remain observations rather than obstacles or trophies
creativeFingerprint.round2Grammar: route cue -> recall beat -> target -> map/point/shape gesture
creativeFingerprint.sectionContrast: Verses stay sparse; chorus widens; retrieval strips back. soft bell sparkle after targets over a warm acoustic pulse
creativeFingerprint.signatureColor: soft bell sparkle after targets over a warm acoustic pulse
creativeFingerprint.authorialIntent: Make an Arctic trek a sequence of changing travel conditions: walk on tundra, use sled routes on snow, stop at ice edge, shift to qajaq or umiak on water, and read wildlife without treating expedition as conquest.
creativeFingerprint.lyricIdentity: A child follows a supervised route and changes travel mode when terrain changes; recurring language uses map, route, runner, shore, launch, turn back, safe distance and next leg.
semanticArc: cross snow and ice by route
finish at shore with wildlife left undisturbed
forbiddenGenericLanguage: find the icy clues with me
